1. Executive summary

The Project Operations Digital Twin is a Mendix application that models a real two-phase, five-school digital transformation program and converts its raw engineering activity into governed, AI-assisted decision support. It fuses two data disciplines that are usually reported separately — traditional project management (schedule, cost, risk, milestones) and DORA software delivery metrics (deploy frequency, lead time, change fail rate, recovery time, rework rate) — into a single Command Center, then uses Claude to correlate signals across both and surface what a program manager should investigate next.

The application is deliberately built around one non-negotiable principle: Claude analyzes, but never decides. Every AI call is a single, stateless request — no tools, no autonomous loop, no memory of previous runs — and every response is stored as a labeled, timestamped, advisory artifact that a human reviews before any action is taken. This is not a limitation of the build; it is the architecture's central design commitment.

This document describes the system as built and deployed: the domain model and why each entity exists, the microflow logic behind data import and DORA calculation, the Claude REST integration end to end, the security model enforced at every layer, and the business case for a director-level technology leadership audience.

2. System architecture overview

The application is organized into three Mendix modules, each with a distinct responsibility. This separation keeps the structural project record, the delivery telemetry, and the AI advisory layer independently secured, independently testable, and independently extensible — a deliberate architectural choice rather than a default.

ModuleEntitiesResponsibility
ProjectCoreProject, Phase, Milestone, Risk, Issue, ProjectDocumentThe project's structural truth — traditional PM artifacts, entered by hand and imported.
TelemetryTelemetrySnapshot, DORADeploymentWeekly health signals and the software-delivery deployment log the five DORA metrics are calculated from.
AI_AgentAIRecommendation (+ REST-mapping entities)The Claude integration and every stored analysis, kept isolated from the data it analyzes.

Layering runs consistently top to bottom across all three modules: a persistable domain model at the base, microflows that own every write and every external call above it, pages that are strictly presentation, and a security layer enforced at the entity, page, and microflow level simultaneously — not just hidden in the UI.

2.1 Why the data is split this way

Project = the two-phase program. Phase = Phase 1 (Infrastructure & School Modernization, completed) and Phase 2 (Digital Learning & School Management Platform, in progress). Milestone = the five-school rollout within each phase. DORA metrics only populate for Phase 2: Phase 1 was infrastructure delivery, not software delivery, and the data model reflects that honestly rather than forcing a metric where none is meaningful.

3. Domain model, entity by entity

Eight entities across three modules — deliberately collapsed from a larger 15-entity draft to keep the demo honest and maintainable rather than impressive-looking on paper.

3.1 ProjectCore

Project holds one record: the program itself. Phase and Milestone carry the schedule story without needing separate WorkPackage or Activity entities. Risk and Issue are deliberately simple: enumerated Probability/Impact/Exposure and Severity fields drive sorting without a scoring microflow. ProjectDocument specializes System.FileDocument, giving it real upload and download capability with no custom file-handling code — it holds the five governing documents behind the numbers the dashboard shows.

3.2 Telemetry

TelemetrySnapshot is a weekly rollup used to drive the Command Center's trend view. DORADeployment is a single deployment log — status, a rework flag, and two pre-calculated helper columns — rather than four separate DORA entities: a scoping decision that is both less modeling overhead and a more realistic mirror of an actual CI/CD deployment log.

3.3 AI_Agent

AIRecommendation is the only entity a human ever reads directly — full request context, response text, status, and timestamp, a complete auditable record of every analysis ever run. Root, Content, ClaudeRequest, and Messages are REST response-mapping entities that exist purely as integration plumbing.

4. Data import architecture

Two different import strategies are used deliberately, matched to two different data-integrity requirements.

4.1 ProjectCore — upsert on natural key

Project, Phase, Milestone, Risk, and Issue are re-importable without ever creating duplicates. Each entity's Import Mapping uses "Find an object (by key)" on its own natural ID — a re-import updates existing records in place. Child entities resolve their parent through a retrieve-and-loop pattern rather than a called sub-microflow, a choice made after an alternative approach produced unresolved parameter-binding issues.

A single button calls one orchestrator microflow, running five imports in dependency order — Project, Phase, Milestone, Risk, Issue — and returning one consolidated message. Every import runs a stray-record cleanup step immediately after the raw JSON import, deleting any record whose key attribute is empty.

4.2 Telemetry — clear and reload

TelemetrySnapshot and DORADeployment use a clear-then-reimport strategy, since these are append-only operational logs rather than hand-edited entities. A companion Admin-only "Delete Telemetry & DORA Data" control prevents the duplication this pattern would otherwise risk on a repeated import click.

4.3 Administrative safeguards

Two scoped delete tools exist, deliberately kept separate — one for ProjectCore data, one for Telemetry/DORA data. Both are Administrator-only, both require on-screen confirmation, and both explicitly exclude AIRecommendation and ProjectDocument: a stored analysis history and uploaded governing documents should never be a side effect of resetting the demo dataset.

5. DORA calculation engine

ACT_CalculateDORAMetrics computes all five DORA metrics from the single DORADeployment log: Deployment Frequency, Median Lead Time and Recovery Time, Change Fail Rate, and Rework Rate.

The microflow branches explicitly on total deployment count before dividing: an empty or newly-reset dataset returns a clean zero-value result instead of a runtime division error — a small detail with an outsized effect on demo reliability.

6. Command Center — page walkthrough

Command Center is the home page for both roles and the single screen the demo's golden path runs through, composed of independently-sourced data views rather than one monolithic query.

SectionData sourceVisible to
Project & phase statusDatabase, bound to the Project recordBoth roles
DORA metricsMicroflow — ACT_CalculateDORAMetricsBoth roles
Overall Health trendDatabase, TelemetrySnapshot sorted by SnapshotDate, Line chart widgetBoth roles
Risks & Issues panelsDatabase, List views on Risk / Issue, Badge widget conditional on Exposure / SeverityBoth roles
AI Analysis & RecommendationMicroflow-triggered write, database-read on displayBoth roles
Data Import / Delete toolsN/A — microflow buttonsAdministrator only

The AI Analysis panel is the centerpiece: one button call to ACT_AnalyzeProjectHealth, a result that renders in place without a manual refresh, and a visible timestamp on every analysis. Risk and Issue summaries now surface directly on Command Center rather than on separate pages — full detail still lives on their own dedicated pages, but the two highest-signal panels are visible without navigating away.

6.1 Delivery trend and risk correlation, on one screen

Below the five DORA tiles, a Line chart plots the Project's OverallHealth score across its eight most recent TelemetrySnapshot records, sorted by SnapshotDate. The chart renders with visible markers at each data point and a plain-language title in place of a legend, since a single-series chart doesn't need one to disambiguate. Alongside it, two List views — one bound to Risk, one to Issue — each render a Badge widget per record, colour-coded by Exposure (Risk) or Severity (Issue). The badge's colour is a design-time property rather than a bindable expression, so each tier is a separate Badge instance gated by a conditional Visibility expression on the enumeration value — proven first in an isolated throwaway app before being promoted here, exactly the same pattern used for the rest of this build's higher-risk UI work.

7. Claude AI integration

The integration is intentionally minimal: one Consumed REST Service, one prompt-building microflow, one advisory response. No agent loop, no tool use, no persistence of conversation state between calls.

7.1 Connection and authentication

A Consumed REST Service points at https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages, POST, with the API key held in a private App Constant — never hard-coded, never exposed to end users — sent as the x-api-key header. The request body uses Mendix's "Use as template (add parameters)" mode with a single {prompttext} placeholder, after a nested-entity body approach produced a CE0117 mapping error.

7.2 Prompt construction

ACT_AnalyzeProjectHealth assembles one string covering project health status, the four category scores, open critical risk/issue counts, and all five DORA numbers — followed by an instruction block directing Claude to identify the two or three most important signals, explain why they matter together, separate observed fact from interpretation, and stop short of a decision.

7.3 Handling the real response shape

Claude's response is not always a single text block — when extended thinking is used, the API returns a content list with a reasoning block ahead of the answer. An early version took the first content item unconditionally, intermittently producing a blank recommendation. The fix filters the content list for the item where type = 'text' before extracting it — correct regardless of which response shape a given call returns.

7.4 Human-in-the-loop by construction, not by policy

  • Every call is single-shot: no tools, no multi-step loop, no memory of prior runs.
  • Every response — success or failure — is written to AIRecommendation with a status, a timestamp, and the full prompt that produced it.
  • Claude has no write access to any operational entity. It reads a snapshot and returns text; it cannot change a Risk, a Milestone, or a DORA number.
  • The prompt itself instructs Claude to stop at investigation, not decision — the interface reinforces the same boundary in its own copy.
This is the load-bearing architectural claim of the whole application: AI provides the analysis, the project manager owns the decision. Every design choice above exists to make that sentence true in the running system, not just in the pitch.

8. Security model

Security level is set to Production across the app — not Prototype/Demo — meaning every entity, page, and microflow is checked against an explicit access rule rather than defaulting open.

Module roleProject / Phase / MilestoneRisk / IssueTelemetry / DORA
ProjectManagerRead; Write on Phase/MilestoneRead, Write, CreateRead
AppAdministratorFullFullFull

AIRecommendation grants ProjectManager Read and Create — trigger and view an analysis, never edit or delete one. ProjectDocument grants Read, Write, Create, so they can contribute governing documents, not just view them. Data Import and both delete tools are Administrator-only at the navigation, page, and microflow level simultaneously, verified against the live Cloud deployment under both roles independently.

9. Business value and customer impact

This application answers a question most utility technology organizations ask separately, and rarely together: is the project on schedule and on budget, and is the engineering work behind it actually healthy? Fusing traditional PM reporting with DORA — an industry-respected, widely adopted software delivery framework — into one Command Center, with AI correlating across both, is a materially stronger technology-leadership story than either discipline reported in isolation.

9.1 What it demonstrates for a director-level review

  • Fluency across the full stack a technology leader is accountable for: data modeling, integration architecture, security, and applied AI.
  • A working, defensible position on AI governance: advisory-only, fully auditable, zero autonomous write access.
  • Real engineering judgment under real constraints: the upsert-versus-clear-reload decision, the thinking-block content fix, the CE0117 REST body resolution — each a genuine trade-off made and documented.

9.2 Customer and operational impact

For a program manager, the practical effect is fewer surprises and faster investigation: a single screen surfaces converging signals — rising lead time alongside rising change failure rate, for instance — that would otherwise sit in two different reports read by two different people on two different cadences. For an organization evaluating a broader platform investment, the twin demonstrates the pattern at low risk before committing to the fuller agentic AI platform it deliberately mirrors.

The application does not claim to replace program management judgment. It claims to make that judgment faster to exercise and easier to defend — every recommendation is timestamped, stored, and traceable back to the exact data that produced it.
